title: Ordered lens decomposition
statement: Two equal-length paths whose common vertices occur in the same order decompose into a series of lens pairs (ri,si), with total signed imbalance sum_i(ri-si)=0.

title: Equal-arm lens elimination
statement: In an ordered equal-length certificate pair chosen with a minimum number of lenses, no nonfatal lens has equal arm lengths.

title: Proper zero-sum block exclusion
statement: In a minimum-lens ordered equal-length pair, no nonempty proper consecutive block of lens imbalances has sum zero.

title: Distinct lens partial sums
statement: For the imbalance sequence of LC03, the partial sums before the final return to zero are pairwise distinct and nonzero.

title: Mixed-route cube theorem
statement: In an ordered lens chain, independently choosing either arm in every lens yields a simple route. Relative to a baseline route of length q, choosing the alternate arms in I gives length q-sum_{i in I}(ri-si).

title: Dyadic subset-sum criterion
statement: If the mixed routes close through one fixed edge, a dyadic cycle of length 2^j occurs whenever a lens-imbalance subset sums to q+1-2^j.

title: The (5,5,6) packet contains C8
statement: The lens packet with arm pairs (3,2),(3,2),(2,4) necessarily contains an 8-cycle.

title: Unit-imbalance kill
statement: Any ordered equal-exponent lens chain containing a lens with |ri-si|=1 contains a cycle of the baseline dyadic length q.

title: Unit subset-sum exclusion
statement: In a counterexample, neither 1 nor -1 is a subset sum of the lens imbalances in an ordered equal-exponent chain.

title: Corrected lens-mass identity
statement: If the two Mersenne certificate paths share h edges, the sum of all lens-cycle lengths in their symmetric difference is 2(q-h).

title: Two-lens arithmetic survivor
statement: The bare two-lens arm pairs (4,1) and (4,7), closed by one edge, generate route-cycle lengths 9,6,12,9 and no power-of-two cycle inside the bare packet.

title: Lens arithmetic alone is insufficient
statement: Perimeter, parity, zero-sum imbalance, and mixed-route arithmetic alone do not eliminate every lens packet.

title: Radius-one completion arguments are incomplete
statement: Checking only chords, cross-edges, and shared immediate outside neighbors does not exhaust minimum-degree completion of a lens packet.

title: Crossed-order cycle extraction
statement: If two common vertices occur in opposite orders along two simple paths, the union of the intervening path segments contains a simple cycle.

title: Two-lens cancellation schema
statement: For two series-realizable lenses with arm pairs (r1,s1),(r2,s2) and equal total route lengths, the crossed totals r1+s2 and s1+r2 are equal and support an equal-length rerouting with fewer lenses.

title: Hostile imbalance compression theorem
statement: Every zero-sum lens-imbalance sequence avoiding all dyadic subset-sum targets compresses by legal route exchanges to a two-lens sequence (d,-d).

title: Secondary-ear lens-collapse theorem
statement: Every ordered minimum-lens equal-exponent certificate pair in a minimum-degree-3 counterexample has a secondary ear that either creates a dyadic cycle or yields a pair with fewer lenses.

title: Crossed-to-ordered reduction
statement: Every crossed equal-exponent certificate pair either contains a dyadic extracted cycle or can be replaced by an ordered pair of no greater complexity.

title: Same-scale near-dyadic overlap theorem
statement: A sufficiently large family of suppression cycles of one length q+1 either contains a pair generating q or 2q, or has a reducible laminar common core.

title: Equal-exponent local close
statement: Any equal exponent occurring in two incident Mersenne certificate spectra at one cubic center forces a power-of-two cycle.

title: General two-lens deficit count
statement: A two-lens packet with arm lengths a,b,c,d and base-connector length r has a+b+c+d+r-5 internal degree-two vertices.

title: Direct-edge conflict spectrum
statement: Adding a packet nonedge uv is individually fatal whenever the packet has a simple u-v path of length 2^k-1.

title: Common-hub conflict spectrum
statement: Two packet vertices u,v cannot share an outside hub neighbor if the packet has a simple u-v path of length 2^k-2.

title: Adjacent-hub conflict spectrum
statement: If hubs z1,z2 are adjacent, u in N(z1), and v in N(z2), then a packet u-v path of length 2^k-3 is forbidden.

title: Hub-neighborhood independence theorem
statement: Every packet neighborhood of one hub is an independent set in the common-hub conflict graph defined by HP03.

title: Two-hub overlap bound
statement: In a C4-free graph, two distinct hubs have at most one common packet neighbor.

title: Hub coverage necessary bound
statement: For N hubs, the number of covered deficit vertices is at most the maximum union of N independent sets in the hub-conflict graph with pairwise intersections at most one.

title: Individual safety is only necessary
statement: A set of packet completion edges may consist entirely of individually safe edges and still jointly create a power-of-two cycle.

title: Cycle-template characterization
statement: For a fixed base configuration B, a candidate edge set F creates a forbidden cycle C iff F contains every edge of C absent from the base graph.

title: Minimal forbidden hyperedge characterization
statement: The canonical forbidden hyperedges are exactly the inclusion-minimal nonempty absent-edge sets F(C) of forbidden cycles after individually unsafe singleton candidates are removed.

title: Forbidden-hyperedge rank bound
statement: If forbidden cycles have length at most L, every minimal forbidden hyperedge has rank at most L; after singleton removal, residual ranks are at least 2.

title: Explicit minimal three-edge obstruction
statement: For the fixed (4,1)oplus(4,7) packet, edges x0-w1, v1-u3, and v3-u1 are pairwise C4/C8-safe but jointly create the C8 x0-w1-x2-v3-u1-u2-u3-v1-x0.

title: Pairwise conflict graph is incomplete
statement: The pairwise conflict graph on individually safe completion edges is not a complete model of residual compatibility.

title: Monotone CNF completion equivalence
statement: For a fixed hub configuration, residual C4/C8-free degree completion is equivalent to a monotone CNF with one positive coverage clause per uncovered deficit vertex and one negative clause per minimal forbidden hyperedge.

title: Hypergraph independent edge-cover theorem
statement: If every feasible N-hub configuration has no candidate-edge set that covers all uncovered deficit vertices while avoiding every forbidden hyperedge, then no C4/C8-free minimum-degree-3 completion with N hubs exists.

title: Candidate-isolation sufficiency
statement: If an uncovered deficit vertex has no incident individually safe candidate edge, the residual completion instance is immediately UNSAT.

title: Exact N=0 candidate set
statement: The fixed 15-vertex packet has exactly 13 individually C4/C8-safe missing edges.

title: Exact N=0 forbidden-hypergraph census
statement: The N=0 candidate hypergraph has exactly 56 minimal forbidden hyperedges: 48 of rank 2 and 8 of rank 3, with none of higher rank.

title: Five unit-forced N=0 edges
statement: At N=0, deficit vertices v1,v3,w2,u5,u6 each have exactly one incident individually safe candidate edge.

title: Compact N=0 hypergraph contradiction
statement: N=0 completion is impossible because coverage forces edges v3-u1 and v2-w2, while that pair is a rank-2 forbidden hyperedge.

title: N=0 packet UNSAT
statement: No simple graph on the 15 packet vertices contains the fixed packet, has minimum degree at least 3, and avoids C4 and C8.

title: Complete N=1 hub-configuration census
statement: There are exactly 21 complete one-hub base configurations that are C4/C8-free and give the hub degree at least 3.

title: Complete N=2 hub-configuration census
statement: There are exactly 24 complete two-hub base configurations: 16 with nonadjacent hubs and 8 with adjacent hubs.

title: N=2 adjacency split
statement: The 24 complete N=2 configurations split exactly into 16 nonadjacent-hub and 8 adjacent-hub configurations.

title: N=1 candidate-isolation theorem
statement: Every one of the 21 complete N=1 configurations leaves an uncovered deficit vertex with no incident individually C4/C8-safe candidate edge.

title: N=2 candidate-isolation theorem
statement: Every one of the 24 complete N=2 configurations leaves an uncovered deficit vertex with no incident individually C4/C8-safe candidate edge.

title: Bounded packet realization lower bound
statement: Any C4/C8-free minimum-degree-3 completion of the fixed packet requires at least three added vertices.

title: Exact deficit conflict-graph edge count
statement: The common-hub conflict graph on the 12 deficit vertices has exactly 40 edges.

title: Exact hub-capacity theorem
statement: The deficit conflict graph has independence number 4 and unique maximum independent set {v1,v2,u1,u2}.

title: Exact two-hub coverage theorem
statement: Two hub neighborhoods that are independent in the deficit conflict graph and overlap in at most one vertex cover at most seven deficit vertices; the maximizing pair is uniquely {v1,v2,u1,u2} and {w3,u4,u5}, up to order.

title: Exact distance-three exclusion count
statement: The fixed packet has exactly 26 nonedges whose endpoints have shortest packet distance 3; every such direct edge creates a C4.

title: Canonical candidate-isolation witness object
statement: The canonical serialized witness object for all 21 N=1 and 24 N=2 configurations has SHA-256 fe2adefe67664121baaf3b8b4a6cf7cafaa5a62ebcc7c8fb2a69ca41aa2ac179 and every record contains at least one isolated uncovered deficit vertex.

title: Human candidate-isolation class theorem
statement: The 45 machine-certified N=1/N=2 configurations admit a short exhaustive human classification in which explicit length-3 or length-7 paths block every missing edge incident to one named uncovered vertex.
